articles.title: 18 Years Later, The Definitive 2000s Gothic Cult Classic is Still a Divisive Guilty Pleasure
articles.summary: The anime equivalent of Twilight also centers on a messy love triangle in a dark supernatural world, but it takes its story to even more controversial places. Based on Matsuri Hino’s classic shojo manga, the 2008 Studio Deen anime Vampire Knight is a unique relic of the late 2000s.
body: Twilight became a cultural phenomenon in part because it tapped into the adolescent fantasy of all-consuming first love. The messy, often toxic love triangle at the center of Twilight only enhanced its appeal, with Bella Swan serving as a relatable blank-slate protagonist caught between a vampire and a werewolf.

Like Twilight, it is a quintessential gothic romance that uses its dark academia setting to explore identity, class, trauma, and prejudice. The lore gets creepy and convoluted, deliberate in its intent to shock and entertain.

A girl named Yuki is attacked by vampires one winter night, but she is rescued by Kaname Kuran, a charismatic Pureblood vampire. Years later, Yuki becomes the guardian of Cross Academy, which reserves its Day classes for humans and Night classes for vampires. As Principal Kaien Cross’ adopted daughter, Yuki takes on the responsibility of protecting the Day class students in service of preserving the peace between the two species.
points: The anime equivalent of Twilight also centers on a messy love triangle in a dark supernatural world, but it takes its story to even more controversial places.
Based on Matsuri Hino’s classic shojo manga, the 2008 Studio Deen anime Vampire Knight is a unique relic of the late 2000s.

articles.title: Rockstar Games employees have locked in a union vote next month, and it'll take place over Grand Theft Auto 6's release window
articles.summary: A date has been locked in for Rockstar Games employees to vote on whether to recognise their developer union. If successful, it will become the largest recognised union across the entirety of the UK video games industry.
body: The vote, which runs from the 12th to the 26th November, will give workers at Rockstar Games a chance to decide whether Rockstar will formally acknowledge and negotiate with the Rockstar Game Workers Union on matters involving its employees. These dates notably fall on either side of Grand Theft Auto 6 's release date, and shortly after Rockstar's head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe told Bloomberg: "we go where the team goes. So if they want a union, they will have a union."

This announcement also comes as the legal battle between Rockstar and the Independent Workers of Great Britain union over the alleged unfair firing of over 30 employees. The union argues this was an attempt at union busting, whereas Rockstar stands by its decision to fire them for gross misconduct, pointing to the sharing of confidential information in a union Discord as the reason for the intervention.
This case was meant to have finished already. However, it ran long, resulting in its conclusion being delayed to the 17th and 18th of November.
points: A date has been locked in for Rockstar Games employees to vote on whether to recognise their developer union.
If successful, it will become the largest recognised union across the entirety of the UK video games industry.

articles.title: GTA 6 is a massive 210GB download on PlayStation 5
articles.summary: There wasn't really any chance Grand Theft Auto 6 wasn't going to be a big download. Thanks to some new information, though, we now have a hard number.
body: PlayStation Game Size, which tracks PS Store game releases by poking through its backend, has revealed that GTA 6 has a chonky 210GB download size. While the actual space it's going to occupy on your console's SSD may be smaller, everyone will have to download over 200GB to play Rockstar's latest.

It's unclear whether GTA 6 is going to require a day one patch on top, or if it's already included in the 210GB. Given the interest in the game, the same PS Store sleuths will no doubt return to update us if the file size changes.

GTA 6 is expected to be one of the most dense games ever in sheer content. It has a highly-detailed, massive open-world map featuring a big number of side activities beyond what most contemporary games offer. The cinematic, hours-long story is the other element that contributes to that massive file size.

articles.title: Legendary Sci-Fi Director's 129-Minute War-Action Masterpiece Is Being Cut From Netflix
articles.summary: When legendary director Paul Verhoeven's space action epic arrived in theaters 29 years ago, a lot of people didn’t get it. While the original 1959 novel by Robert A. Heinlein had a militaristic right-wing viewpoint, Verhoeven and screenwriter Edward Neumeier sought to lampoon those themes when…
body: Over the years, Starship Troopers has been reevaluated as a sharp piece of commentary, not dissimilar to Verhoeven and Neumeier’s other sci-fi satire, RoboCop. Nearly three decades later, Starship Troopers ’s themes remain sharp. Additionally, its exciting fight scenes and uniquely-designed aliens make it fun to watch even without the political commentary, which is why it's worth a revisit now before it leaves Netflix at the end of October.

Brought to life with both practical effects and CGI, the look of the aliens in Starship Troopers is one of the most impressive things about the film. The massive, killer “arachnids” have unique designs clearly inspired by the bugs of Earth, but way bigger, and with clamp-like mandibles for a head. While some of the bigger bugs suffer from the limitations of late 1990s CGI, they're all still interesting and menacing.

articles.title: 5 Funniest 'Peanuts' Comics About Snoopy's Forgotten Siblings
articles.summary: Charles Schulz's Snoopy is one of the most famous fictional dogs in the world, if not the most famous. His only real competition might be Goofy, who's apparently supposed to be an anthropomorphic dog (which, as ever, raises some real uncomfortable questions about Pluto), or possibly Scooby-Doo.
body: Snoopy is one of the oldest characters in Peanuts, first appearing in its third-ever strip in 1950. For the first few years of the comic, Snoopy might've been a stray who was broadly adopted by the neighborhood kids, as he seemed to belong to whichever kid he had to in order for the latest joke to work. It wasn't until 1972 that Schulz finally established that Snoopy belonged to Charlie Brown.

That's a useful example of an overall trend with Snoopy, who has the longest character arc in Peanuts. By the time the strip ended in 2000, Snoopy had evolved from a fairly normal beagle to a struggling writer with a number of elaborate fantasy personae, a penchant for walking upright, a doghouse that's basically a TARDIS, an ambiguous ability to communicate directly with humans, and his own extensive supporting cast.

In addition to his bird pal Woodstock, Snoopy has seven brothers and sisters, most of whom were rarely seen in Peanuts. The exception is Spike, Snoopy's desert-dwelling brother, who went from a brief visit in 1975 to a regular fixture in the comic by the '90s.
points: Charles Schulz's Snoopy is one of the most famous fictional dogs in the world, if not the most famous.
His only real competition might be Goofy, who's apparently supposed to be an anthropomorphic dog (which, as ever, raises some real uncomfortable questions about Pluto), or possibly Scooby-Doo.

articles.title: Masahiro Sakurai Shrugs Off AI Games as ‘Unprofitable Titles’ as Clones and Mods Boom
articles.summary: Super Smash Bros creator Masahiro Sakurai explained why the boom in AI-created games isn’t likely to create a lasting demand for such projects, comparing them to “low-quality goods” that could never compare to human-made titles like Shadow of the Colossus.
body: Sakurai made these remarks in an interview with Denfaminico Gamer after he was asked for his thoughts on the huge boom in games that have been released on Steam since 2010. The interviewer noted that, since 2010, this amount skyrocketed from 275 titles to 19,000 titles.

“19,000 is amazing, but I think that number will increase even more from now on. I'm sure of it. That's because AI will increase the number. However, I think most of them will become ‘unprofitable titles.’ There are too many to keep track of, and it's impossible to understand them all,” he said.

“When it comes to things created with AI... or things mass-produced with poor quality, I think most of them will simply be reproductions of systems seen in various other games. I think there are already a lot of those now.”

He went on to mention conceptually simple games that fall into the puzzle genre, even calling out the viral Needle in a Haystack Simulator as part of his example. According to Sakurai, these types of games are easy for AI to recreate, as artificial intelligence cannot make something original, but only iterate on what has come before.

articles.summary: In Buffy the Vampire Slayer, Halloween is the one night a year when monsters think it’s cliché to go out and torment the Hellmouth. As Buffy elegantly puts it: Halloween is “like, dead for the undead.” But 29 years ago, one evildoer decided to wreak havoc in Sunnydale on the one night no one…
body: “Halloween” aired on Oct. 27, 1997, as the sixth episode of season 2. Written by Carl Ellsworth and directed by Bruce Seth Green, it’s the show’s first Halloween episode and its first holiday episode in general. It's also an important one for Buffy as a whole, coming in as the series was establishing its tone after a rocky first season. "Halloween" represented an upswing in its viewership, drawing almost 6 million viewers (a million more than the previous episode). It was also a rare instance of Buffy being rendered helpless, forcing the show's ensemble cast to rise up to the challenge, establishing some of the patterns they would follow in future seasons.

“Halloween” follows Ethan Rayne (Robin Sachs), a recurring villain from Giles' past, as he arrives in Sunnydale and opens a costume shop just in time for the holiday. He then calls on the two-faced god, Janus, cursing anyone who buys an outfit to become that character on Halloween night.

articles.title: Creator of Viral Needle in a Haystack Game Roasts Copycats With 'Find the Original Game' Mode
articles.summary: The creator of a viral indie game where players must literally find a needle in a haystack is tired of his project getting cloned. So, he made a new game mode, where players must find the real game in a pile of fakes.
body: Thanks to advancements in artificial intelligence, it’s getting easier and easier for players to 'reverse-engineer' video games and even outright copy projects that haven’t been released yet.

It’s been a hellish situation for developers in the industry, particularly for small studios without the funds for legal backing or, even worse, single creators who made their games all by themselves.

NasNakarus is the driving mind behind Needle in a Haystack Simulator, which is exactly what it sounds like. Such a simple concept is easy to copy, and there are currently oodles of similar titles clogging online marketplaces. But he’s not taking it personally; instead, he’s poking fun at the ordeal with some well-timed commentary and a new ‘mode’ for his game.

articles.title: You Can Make Your WoW: Forever Character Now And Be Ready For Launch
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever's character creation and name reservations are now live, letting you save some time on launch day by making your characters now rather than on launch day.
body: To access name reservations, you'll need to have Forever preinstalled on Battle.net and have purchased at least the $30 Skyborne Heroic Pack, which grants access to the game's new optional playable race, the Skyborne elves. Once you've done that, you can simply log into the game, select the ruleset you want to play on, and create your characters.

You can create and name up to three characters ahead of launch day. Unlike in other versions of developer Blizzard's MMORPG, Forever requires both a first name and last name for characters, giving you more options and creative freedom when it comes to names.

When making a character, make sure you create them on the server ruleset you intend to play on. Once the game is live, Blizzard said there won't be a way to transfer characters to different rulesets. It's also worth noting that on player vs. player rulesets, you will only be able to create characters of a single faction on that specific ruleset, so make your choice of Alliance or Horde wisely.

articles.title: GTA 6 Developers Are About To Do Something Historic
articles.summary: Workers at GTA 6 developer Rockstar will soon get to vote on recognizing a union. The union, IWGB Union at Rockstar, is for Rockstar's UK-based developers. Rockstar North, based in Edinburgh, Scotland, is one of Rockstar's biggest outfits in the UK, and the lead developer on GTA 6.
body: The negotiating process between the union and Rockstar management took months, and the union, if recognized, would give workers a stronger seat at the table for key issues like pay and bonuses, overtime, generative AI policies, work-from-home setups, and situations involving layoffs.
The IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union would become the largest in the UK video game sector, if it's voted in.
The voting period--November 12-26--overlaps with the release of GTA 6 on November 19.

At the same time, an employment tribunal over claims that Rockstar fired developers for trying to form a union is coming to a close, with final arguments set for November 17 and November 18. More than 30 IWGB members were let go from Rockstar in the UK in October 2025, with the union saying Rockstar fired them for trying to form a union. Rockstar, for its part, said the staffers were dismissed for leaking key details about Rockstar's upcoming games.

articles.title: Part idle game, part automation game, Moon Sweepers exploits the sickness in me that adores both Satisfactory and Cookie Clicker
articles.summary: When Edwin talked about Moon Sweepers yesterday he focused on the artisanal approach to space rock cleaning. Like the puritan he is, he wants to wipe away all the dust on the moon using a toothbrush.
body: But then I got down to the serious business of trying to clean up the dusty moon, section by section and all thoughts of art left my head.

When you first begin Moon Sweepers, you're faced with an entire planetoid broken down into hexagonal tiles, each deep with dust and needing a brushing. The first sectors you'll clean take an age to clear. The toothbrush only carves a thin groove into the dirt and the tile is comparatively vast. Your backpack fills with hoovered up dust as you clean and when it's filled you need to head back to base to sell it off. Each kilo sold nets you a single dollar, but with that cash you can buy improved tools, swapping your toothbrush for a hand brush, and eventually for a broom.
It was only after I bought my broom I realised – too late to save myself – that I was playing an incremental game.

articles.title: Official WoW: Forever AMV Will Get You Super Hyped
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever is almost here, and in case players weren't already excited to return to classic Azeroth, a new animated music video highlighting the war between the Horde and the Alliance is sure to get your inner player vs. player hyped up to spill some blood for your faction.
body: Called "Warpath," the animated trailer made in collaboration between developer Blizzard and Brunch Studio features a banger of a track performed by YouTuber turned musician Poppy, Amy Lee of Evanescence fame, and Courtney LaPlante, the lead singer of Canadian metal band Spiritbox. The name of the song itself is "End of You," and its nu-metal vibes go a long way to invoke the early 2000s era that WoW originally spawned from.

The trailer shows members of the Horde (an orc Rogue, tauren Hunter, undead Paladin, troll Mage) and the Alliance (a human Warrior, gnome Warlock, dwarf Shaman, night elf Priest, and Skyborne Druid) duking it out on the slopes of Mount Hyjal, one of Forever's new zones.

Each class is wearing their iconic endgame dungeon armor set and can be seen wielding more than a few recognizable weapons, like Unstoppable Force, Dal'Rend's Sacred Charge and Tribal Guardian, and others.

It's not the first time Blizzard has collaborated with Brunch on an AMV. Blizzard released "A Place To Call Home" performed by Aurora earlier this year ahead of the release of modern WoW's Midnight expansion, and it was quite the walk down memory lane for longtime players.

videos.title: The Wolf Among Us Remastered Review
videos.summary: The Wolf Among Us Remastered reviewed by Sarah Thwaites on PC, also available on Xbox, PlayStation, and Switch.
body: "The Wolf Among Us Remastered revamps Telltale’s beloved episodic adventure, adding neon highlights to its already vivid world full of complex characters. While the pacing still dips slightly toward the end, nuanced performances and heart-pounding quick-time events quickly reel you back in as you bear down on the killer. It’s disappointing that some of the original’s stiff animations haven't been ironed out, but the stunning environmental redesigns and a solid suite of bonus features more than make up for it. Though not entirely definitive, this remaster is a powerful reminder of why The Wolf Among Us earned its acclaim – and with a sequel on the horizon, it's a brilliant way to either revisit or catch up on a neo-noir mystery that still deserves its flowers."
points: The Wolf Among Us Remastered reviewed by Sarah Thwaites on PC, also available on Xbox, PlayStation, and Switch.
